title: Your Stomach Acid Can Dissolve Metal — So Why Doesn't It Eat You? 🤯
script: This acid dissolves metal — and your body produces it every single hour. Your stomach generates hydrochloric acid at pH 1.5 — corrosive enough to burn through living tissue. Every time you digest food, your stomach should be destroying itself from the inside. But here's the wild part — every 3 hours, your stomach rebuilds its entire protective mucus lining, replacing it before the acid burns through. Miss just one cycle, and you get an ulcer. Send this to someone who thinks stress doesn't wreck their body. And that's how.
search_summary: Human stomach produces pH 1.5 hydrochloric acid and rebuilds its mucus lining every 3 hours to avoid self-digestion.
comment_question: So stress literally eats your stomach lining — still think it's 'just in your head'? 🤔
source_note: Physiology of the Gastrointestinal Tract, Elsevier, 2006
